newsitem.title: USA: Luby's comfortable with low end of estimates.
newsitem.headline: Luby's comfortable with low end of estimates.

text.p: Luby's Cafeterias Inc President John Curtis on Tuesday said he is comfortable with the low end of analysts' consensus estimates for the second quarter and year.

"I feel we're within the range of the analysts' estimates," Curtis said of $0.39 to $0.43 a share earnings estimates for the second quarter. But he said the First Call mean estimate of $0.41 a share "may be a little high."
Curtis said First Call's mean $1.76 a share estimate for fiscal 1997 "may be a little on the high side," but said he was comfortable with analysts' $1.70 to $1.80 a share earnings range for the year.

"We feel we are doing well. It's just that we've got some unusual cost situations that we're dealing with now with this major acquisition we made of Wyatt's and the increased minimum wage. We're working through those," Curtis said.
Luby's purchased 20 Wyatt's Cafeterias last summer and reopened 15 as Luby's cafeterias in October.
Luby's Chief Financial Officer Laura Bishop said Wyatt's sales volumes were below those of the typical Luby's outlet.
"It automatically forces your labor up as a percentage of sales because these volumes are a little bit lower," she said. "Next year it will be a much easier comparison."

Luby's Chairman Pete Erben told the annual shareholders meeting the company is seeking to post double-digit sales growth from expansion that will include the opening of 30 cafeterias this year. The company has seen growth in the 6.5 percent range over the past five years.
"If you're going to be rewarded in the stock market, you have to have double-digit growth," he said.
